items.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012
items.q: I have a game with my best friend, John Ramirez back in Chicago

ctx.x: So you just learned about voicing and ranges and all that from listening and talking to the players?

Yes. Trial and error and I’d ask them, I’d say “what’s the highest note you want to hit on a tenor saxophone?” “Well you get to this point and then you hit an altissimo.” “All right, what’s the best range for a trombone? What’s the toughest position?” “Seventh. Stay away from it.” And then Henry Mancini of all people — I was playing a gig in a hotel, quite young, and he walks in. What do you give him? I have a game with my best friend, John Ramirez back in Chicago, we call “what do you give ‘em?” Which means if…

example, if Paul McCartney were to walk in what do you give him? Well I’m not going to give him a Beatle song, I’m not going to even give him a post-Beatle song. I’m going to lay this one on him. Do I have time to give this 30-second anecdote?
